transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-16
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Raj (Redwood SE), Alicia (CSM), Tom (Lyndon CTO), Priya (Platform Lead), Evan (SRE), Nora (Security)

Auto-summary (auto):
Customer is evaluating hosting mode for high-throughput streaming inference (real-time route optimization). Primary goals: p95 <= 120ms for short-form prompts, sustained token throughput during peak windows, secure VPC/private option for PII, clear rollback/fallbacks to smaller model under capacity. They asked for a reproducible p95 streaming benchmark and dedicated capacity pricing.

Topics (auto-tags): latency SLA, p95 targets, concurrency, streaming tokens/sec, hosted vs dedicated vs private, KMS/SSO, audit logs, burst capacity, KV cache, fallback policies

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood — I'm AE on this account. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Tom: Hi Tom here, CTO at Lyndon Logistics. We have Priya, Evan and Nora on.
[00:10] Priya: Priya — platform lead.
[00:12] Evan: Evan, SRE.
[00:14] Nora: Nora, security.
[00:16] Raj: Raj Patel, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll mostly dive into perf and benchmarks.
[00:20] Maya: Cool, high level agenda: understand your p95 targets, traffic shape and then walk through hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private VPC) and what a benchmark would look like.
[00:29] Tom: We're trying to decide between hosted for speed of integration vs dedicated or private because of customer data. Our app is route optimization, lots of short prompts, a few long holds. p95 is the main SLA number for product. We aim for p95 under 120ms for generation on our 256-token-ish prompts, and sustained concurrency up to 200 QPS at peak.
[00:48] Raj: OK got it. When you say 256 tokens are you counting the full seq len output plus prompt?
[00:52] Priya: Typically prompt+response ~ 220 tokens, we budget for 256 as upper bound. Most responses are streaming token output — so we care about first byte p95 and also end-to-end completion p95 for billing reasons.
[01:08] Raj: Right, Redwood supports streaming first-token latency and continuous streaming for the rest. For hosted, our baseline for a ~200 token completion on default models hits first-byte p95 ~70-90ms on our benchmarks, but that varies with seq-length and batch size. For dedicated you can get more consistent p95 and predictable token/sec throughput because you reserve GPU pools and reduce noisy neighbors.
[01:34] Evan: Our concern is noisy neighbors on hosted causing p95 spikes during business hours; we need predictable latency for SLAs. Also cost is a factor — dedicated looks expensive.
[01:44] Maya: Totally. Dedicated is about cost of reserved capacity but you trade that for predictable tail latency. We also have autoscaling and burst policies so you can reserve a baseline and allow bursts to hosted capacity if you want — hybrid routing.
[01:58] Priya: Hybrid sounds promising. How's the fallback route if dedicated hits saturation? How fast is a region-level failover?
[02:05] Raj: Failovers depend on routing policy. Canary or auto-fallback can route to hosted compatible model variants in under a few 100ms for new requests, but current in-flight streaming completions might get cut off. We recommend prefix/KV cache and graceful degrade where fallback returns a smaller model variant.
[02:22] Tom: Can you quantify p95 impact if we fall back to a smaller quantized model?
[02:28] Raj: Roughly you drop CPU/GPU work and p95 can improve 20–40% on token latency but generation quality may degrade. We do model recommendations per workload — Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles.
[02:40] Nora: Security wise, we need to know about encryption, KMS, and audit trails. For Private we need VPC peering and HSM support.
[02:48] Maya: For Private we offer customer-managed VPC, KMS integration, audit logs with retention options and SOC2 artifacts. HSM can be supported via partner integrations; we'll send the security pack.
[02:58] Nora: Also need RBAC and SSO (SAML).
[03:02] Alicia: We support SAML SSO and granular RBAC at route/model level.
[03:06] Evan: Back to perf: What does the benchmark look like? We need token/sec sustained and p95 distribution across 1h windows and 5m windows.
[03:15] Raj: We can provide a benchmark harness that replays your payloads and measures first-byte, last-byte p95, token/sec and concurrency. We'll give you the script plus a sample dataset. We'll run both hosted and dedicated runs. For dedicated we'll instrument GPU utilization (BFC, KV cache hit rates) and for hosted we provide distribution across instances.
[03:34] Priya: We also want burst tests: 10x baseline for 30s to simulate batch route updates.
[03:40] Raj: Good, we typically run ramp tests: steady-state at baseline (200 QPS), 3x sustained for 5 minutes, and 10x for 30s bursts. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and token throughput.
[03:50] Tom: For statistical confidence — how many runs do you do? We prefer multiple runs over different times of day.
[03:55] Raj: We'll do at least 3 runs per mode and advise you to repeat during your peak windows. For hosted we recommend running tests in your chosen region and time-of-day.
[04:04] Evan: What about streaming costs — tokens per second interplay with latency when we enable continuous batching or KV caching.
[04:10] Raj: Right. Batching improves throughput and reduces cost but can add micro-latency. Continuous batching in our runtime dynamically batches only when it meets latency SLOs. KV/prefix caching improves p95 dramatically for repeated prefixes — we saw 30–60% token-cost reductions for chatty sessions. But for route optimization, you may have high variance; caching will help if prompts share prefixes.
[04:30] Priya: Our prompts are mostly distinct but last-mile info repeats (like vehicle state). Maybe partial prefix caching is useful.
[04:36] Raj: We can instrument token-level traces so you can see per-prefix hit rate.
[04:40] Nora: On compliance, how about audit log retention? We need 12 months.
[04:44] Maya: We offer configurable retention; enterprise can get 12+ months.
[04:47] Nora: Great. Also, do you support private on-prem air-gapped?
[04:51] Raj: Yes, Private includes an on-prem package, but that has longer lead time and includes discrete SLAs and support.
[04:57] Tom: Cost again — can you give a ballpark figure for dedicated baseline for our traffic? We estimated 200 QPS peaks with 220 tokens average.
[05:05] Maya: We'll send an estimate in the pricing spreadsheet, but rough ballpark: model choice matters a lot. For a medium-sized open model quantized to 4-bit, a dedicated GPU node can handle X token/sec; to size properly we'll run a capacity planning run. We'll include a token/sec per-GPU table.
[05:24] Priya: For our team, we need p95 under 120ms for first byte and completion p95 under 450ms for full 220 tokens — is that realistic?
[05:33] Raj: First-byte p95 120ms is definitely achievable in dedicated or well-configured hosted; completion p95 depends on tokens/sec generation speed. If model emits tokens at 40–60 tokens/sec, a 220 token completion adds 3.5–5.5s purely for generation — so completion p95 of 450ms suggests you expect streaming to start quickly and perhaps shorter completions. Clarify: do you mean first-byte/response start p95 120ms and tail p95 for initial chunk?
[05:55] Tom: Good point — we mostly care about first-byte p95 for user-perceived latencies. Backend processing that streams following tokens can be slower. So first-byte 120ms target, yes.
[06:05] Raj: Great. Then that is aligned — we'll focus benchmarks on first-byte p95 and sustained token throughput.
[06:10] Evan: Any network egress concerns if we go hosted? We need to ensure region residency.
[06:15] Maya: We host in multiple regions; you can pin region and we support data residency controls for enterprise tiers.
[06:21] Priya: We also want instrumentation — request traces with token-level breakdown and per-route cost.
[06:26] Raj: That's Redwood Console — per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, and trace hooks. We'll show you sample dashboards.
[06:33] Tom: Will the SDKs support streaming reconnects if a connection is lost mid-stream? We need resumption semantics.
[06:39] Raj: We have token-level cursors via the streaming API and recommended client patterns. For guaranteed exactly-once semantics you may need an idempotency layer; we can share SDK examples.
[06:48] Priya: About the engineering kickoff — what do we need to prepare for the pilot?
[06:52] Raj: A sample traffic trace (1–2 hours of typical requests), a short dataset of prompt variants, and an example endpoint in your staging environment. We'll use that to replay workload.
[07:01] Priya: We can provide a 1-hour sample and some synthetic burst scripts.
[07:05] Raj: Perfect. Also, tell us which model you want to benchmark — open model or Redwood-curated?
[07:11] Tom: We prefer an open LLM we already tried, but are open to Redwood suggestions if they improve p95/cost.
[07:18] Raj: We'll include our recommended model variants and quantization profiles. For dedicated runs we'll include GPU-level metrics and KV cache hit rate.
[07:25] Evan: A practical question: how do you price token throughput vs reserved nodes? If we reserve 2 GPUs, can we measure tokens/sec headroom?
[07:31] Maya: The pricing sheet will show reserved node cost, estimated tokens/sec per-node for each recommended model, and a burst allowance to hosted. We also support percent-based overage billing.
[07:41] Tom: We also want a canary plan for deploys so we don't break production on model swaps.
[07:45] Alicia: Rollouts -> we support canary, A/B, and automatic rollback policies. You can pin model versions at route level.
[07:52] Priya: On the KV cache point, is there a way to supply warm prefixes for routes? We would like warm starts for common route templates.
[07:58] Raj: Yes, you can pre-warm KV entries and we expose prewarm APIs in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports prewarming with a short TTL.
[08:06] Nora: Any certification caveats — SOC2 Type II? ISO?
[08:09] Maya: We have SOC2 and are pursuing ISO; we'll include current compliance docs in the security pack.
[08:15] Tom: Great. Can you outline the benchmark deliverables and timeline?
[08:19] Raj: Deliverables: benchmark harness + scripts, hosted run results, dedicated run results (if you sign for trial), detailed p95/p99 histograms, GPU utilization traces, KV cache hit report, and a recommendations doc. Timeline: script by 3/20, runs within 1 week of data + staging endpoint, deliverables within 10 business days after runs.
[08:38] Priya: That works. For acceptance criteria, we want first-byte p95 <= 120ms for 95% of runs and clear token/sec headroom to scale to 400 QPS with burst capacity.
[08:49] Raj: We'll structure tests to measure headroom and map GPUs to QPS for your model.
[08:54] Tom: Anything around throttling/backpressure? If we hit limits will Redwood return 429s or queue?
[08:59] Raj: You can configure per-route qps throttling, and Redwood will return 429 for requests over capacity. There's also a graceful degraded path where you can route to cheaper model variant instead of rejecting.
[09:10] Evan: Could we get token-level cost estimates per 100k tokens for candidate models?
[09:14] Maya: Yes we'll include unit economics in the spreadsheet and examples of batching/caching savings.
[09:20] Priya: For the pilot, we want a private VPC option if we proceed to enterprise. How long to enable a Private deployment?
[09:26] Raj: Private deployments historically take 6–8 weeks depending on networking approvals and HSM work. On-prem air-gapped is longer. We'll provide an onboarding checklist.
[09:36] Tom: OK that timeline is fine. For the immediate next step, send pricing + benchmark script.
[09:41] Maya: Will do. Anything else?
[09:43] Nora: One more security note: we need data deletion policy details and subprocessor list.
[09:48] Maya: We'll include that in the security pack.
[09:50] Priya: Quick UX question — if you route to hosted for bursts, are there routing policies by latency, cost or region?
[09:57] Raj: Yes. Routing policies support latency-first, cost-first or region pinning. You can also do capacity tiers: try dedicated first, then burst to hosted, then fallback to smaller variant.
[10:08] Tom: Great. Let's recap then.
[10:11] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet and SLA matrix, security pack (KMS/HSM, SOC2, audit logs), benchmark harness and sample script by 3/18–3/20. Customer to provide 1hr traffic trace + staging endpoint and identify preferred models. Schedule pilot kickoff week of 3/23.
[10:28] Priya: Confirmed.
[10:30] Tom: Confirmed.
[10:31] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and scheduling poll.

Notes about transcription quality: there are a few mis-heard words (K-V cash shows up in one auto-note), some product names typed as Redwood Inferenc. Natural crosstalk at times, speaker labels were clean.

End of transcript.
